text:
maria_support: Customer reports intermittent 500s on /v1/generate. They provided req_id=req_0a1b2c3d4e. Asking if we can pull server-side logs and confirm retention window. They say it started around 2026-03-14T18:12:30Z and happens ~1-2x /minute.

ben_infra: Got it. Can you confirm the exact request_id (looks truncated) and the region/cluster? Also need the client's timestamp range.

maria_support: Full request_id from customer: req_0a1b2c3d4e5f6789. They hit us from us-west-2. First observed at 2026-03-14T18:12:30Z, latest at 2026-03-14T18:18:05Z.

alex_sre: I'll try a quick search. For Splunk/Kibana we usually run something like:
```
index=prod_edge_logs AND request_id:\"req_0a1b2c3d4e5f6789\" | sort @timestamp
```
If using BigQuery (central logging):
```
SELECT * FROM `redwood-prod.logs_2026*`
WHERE jsonPayload.request_id = \"req_0a1b2c3d4e5f6789\"
AND timestamp BETWEEN \"2026-03-14T18:10:00Z\" AND \"2026-03-14T18:20:00Z\"
ORDER BY timestamp ASC
```

alex_sre: Note retention: edge/access traces are kept 30 days, application request logs (router/runtime) 90 days, and control-plane audit logs 365 days. If the customer is past 30 days we might not have full L7 traces.

sara_engineer: If logs are missing because of rotation, we can still look for correlated traces via the user_id/client_id or the session_id. Any customer account id?

maria_support: Customer account id: acct_42-881. Client reported an x-request-id header value identical to the request_id above.

ben_infra: Helpful. I'm running a cluster-level grep on the node logs (quick tool):
```
grep -R --line-number \"req_0a1b2c4e5f6789\" /var/log/redwood/hosts/* | head -50
```
(typo-safe: searching with wildcard for the middle chunk can find rotated files)

alex_sre: Also try searching the kv-cache debug events and model-worker logs — sometimes 500s come from an OOM in the worker and only appear in worker-output. Example: 
```
grep -R \"req=\"req_0a1b2c3d4e5f6789\"\" /var/log/model-worker/*
```

deploy-bot: deploy v1.12.3 rolled to us-west-2 at 2026-03-14T17:50:02Z on canary-3. No errors flagged by rollout bot.

sara_engineer: For repro, ask the customer to run curl with x-request-id set so we can match server logs:
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer SK-xxxx\" -H \"x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d4e5f6789\" \\n  -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-7b","input":"test prompt"}' \\n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
If they can attach the full response and the corresponding client timestamp, that helps.

maria_support: Customer ran the curl and attached the full response body + client logs. They also uploaded a debug bundle at: https://internal.redwood/debug-bundles/acct_42-881/1797401234.zip

alex_sre: I pulled the bundle. Worker logs show repeated 429 followed by a 500 from the model-worker during streaming. Snippet: 
```
[2026-03-14T18:14:12Z] ERROR model-worker[pid=2345]: write failed: broken pipe, req=req_0a1b2c3d4e5f6789
[2026-03-14T18:14:12Z] WARN kv-cache: miss for prefix 0x7f...
```
Suggests the streaming connection to the client was interrupted, then the worker attempted a retry and hit an internal error.

ben_infra: Can we confirm upstream (proxy) logs for connection resets? Run this to find resets near the timestamp:
```
index=proxy_logs status=RST OR message:\"connection reset\" | where request_id=\"req_0a1b2c3d4e5f6789\" | stats count by host
```

alex_sre: I can see the proxy closed the socket from host ip 10.2.14.7 at 18:14:12. Client reported intermittent NAT issues; could be client-side network flaps.

sara_engineer: Actionable next steps for support: 1) Ask customer to run repeated curl with x-request-id and attach any NAT / proxy logs they have; 2) If they can reproduce, escalate to dedicated capacity team to trace whether worker OOMs coincide with spikes; 3) If logs are missing due to retention, offer to provide a debug snapshot for the last-90d window (if within retention) or explain we can't retrieve beyond 90d for app logs.

maria_support: I'll send the repro request and ask for their edge NAT logs. Also noted retention rules when replying. Assigning owner: alex_sre. Keeping this thread open until customer confirms repro. :thumbsup:
